articles.headline: Our Paper (editorial)
articles.summary: The increase of our paper is such, that we fell short of nearly fifty copies last week. We were very sorry all were not supplied.

articles.summary: Would not each church in the city like to have a standing yearly card in the Recorder, giving the name of the Church and its location, the pastor, the hours of service on Sabbath, prayer-meetings, and Sabbath School, &c.? This, we believe, would add strength to all the churches, especially when strangers come to the city, as it would be a guide to them.

articles.summary: Our esteemed and Rev. Bishop Payne is in our city. We have had the pleasure of his company at the Book Room several times since his arrival. He has been paying Episcopal visits in the western portion of Pennsylvania. We are glad to learn that we shall have the Board of Bishops in this city during the session of our annual Conference, at which time we hope to have some definite understanding about our hymn book.

articles.headline: The Present Crisis (editorial)
articles.summary: America, since the Declaration of Independence, which occurred in 1776, has never experienced such a commotion as has been existing for the last six months -- brother against brother, sister against sister, father against son and daughter, mother against daughter and son, some for a 'dissolution' of the Union, and some for adherence to the Union, and but few for God!

articles.headline: The City Movements (editorial items)
articles.summary: The Board of Controllers of Public Schools held a stated meeting on the afternoon of the 9th inst., Mr. Henry Bumm, President, in the chair. ... There is not a night in the week on which the colored people have not a meeting of some kind. We think a portion of the Bethel Church members belong to more societies than any other class of people in the city. Some of them belong to five, six, and seven societies. St. Thomas' Church and the Brick Wesley Church have been holding Fairs ever since Easter, and St. Thomas' is doing well. The Hutchinson Family sang on behalf of Union A. M. E. Church a few evenings ago.

articles.headline: Meeting of the Conferences
articles.summary: The Ohio Conference meets in Columbus, Ohio, on the 18th inst. Bishop Quinn will preside. ... The Philadelphia Conference meets on the 18th of May, in Union Church, Coates' Street, between Fourth and Fifth Streets. Bishop Nazrey will preside. The New York Conference meets on the 30th of May, in Bridge Street Church, Brooklyn. Bishop Payne will preside. The New England Conference will meet in Providence, R.I., on the 15th [VERIFY] of June. Bishop Nazrey will preside.

bishop; to preside, Ohio and Indiana Conferences (printed 'Bishop Quinn')
bishop; to preside, New York and Baltimore Conferences (printed 'Bishop Payne')

articles.headline: How We Spent Last Sabbath (Bethel Sabbath School and Union Church)
articles.summary: In the morning at Bethel Sabbath School, we heard the children recite their catechism. We must say that we felt a new era had commenced among our young generation. ... At ten o'clock we ascended to the main audience room, and heard the pastor, Rev. J. Woodlin, preach. This was a sacrament morning. ... After he was through, Bishop Payne arose ... and made some very deep and pertinent remarks relative to the priesthood; after which he then proceeded to the consecration of the sacramental elements. ... We had given Brother Schureman word that we would preach for him at three o'clock, it being his last quarterly meeting for this Conference year. At the time appointed we were on hands, and found Union jammed full.
people: bishop; consecrated the elements at Bethel (printed 'Bishop Payne')

articles.headline: News from the Churches
articles.summary: Bishop Payne has handed us a letter to read which he had just received from Rev. John M. Brown of Baltimore ... We have received a very interesting letter from Rev. I. J. Hill, of the Penningtonville Circuit, written from Oxford, informing us of the arrival of Bishop Nazrey, who has been out for some time in his diocese, paying episcopal visits. He spent Easter Sabbath at a point on the circuit called Britten [VERIFY]. ... After the Love Feast was over, the Bishop preached from John vi. 34.

articles.headline: [Letter of Rev. James A. Shorter on the General/Executive Committee]
articles.summary: We have received a letter from Rev. James A. Shorter, who wishes us to insert the following, which is an answer, or a reply to, Revs. Moore and Woodyard: 'The Christian Recorder did not come into existence by the order of the General Committee, J. A. Shorter being a member of the said General Committee.' We endorse brother Shorter's views.

articles.headline: To the Editor of the Christian Recorder (letter praising the paper)
articles.author: Nathaniel Wiggins
articles.summary: Rev. Elisha Weaver -- Dear Brother: It is with pleasure that we see the gigantic strides the Christian Recorder is making under your management. ... and, as our distinguished brother (Rev. Stephen Smith) said at a recent meeting held at our mother-church, Bethel, that he hoped the Christian Recorder might live and never die, to which we heartily respond by saying, Amen.
people: quoted speaker at the Bethel meeting (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter (on an article from 'the Paramount of the Philadelphia District')
articles.author: A. C. Crippen
articles.summary: Rev. Sir, and Editor of the Christian Recorder: I refused to arraign an article coming from the Paramount of the Philadelphia District, touching an article said to come from the Bishop of the New York District. ... I, however, think the advice of the Right Rev. W. Nazrey to be good. I am, Sir, a truly law-abiding minister of the A. M. E. connexion.

articles.author: St. Cyprian

An idea of the object may be briefly set forth by the following extract of a meeting held at Masonic Hall during the latter part of last August. [City of the meeting not stated; probably New York. articles.headline: Our Paper (editorial)
articles.summary: We have been publishing the Recorder regularly since we commenced, and have sent of each issue a copy to all brethren whose address is known to us; -- we mean our ministerial brethren, many of whom have neither countenanced us, by getting subscribers, nor even sent us their own subscriptions. ... when our esteemed and much-loved brethren, Revs. Green, Clark, and Campbell, were editors and General Book Stewards ...

articles.headline: Notice (Grand Social Entertainment for the Christian Recorder)
articles.summary: The Friends of the Christian Recorder, anxious for its welfare and advancement, have thought proper to give an entertainment for the encouragement and advancement of said paper. This grand social entertainment will take place on Wednesday, the first day of May, 1861. ... The choir attached to Bethel Church have kindly volunteered their services. ... The entertainment will be held at the Philadelphia Hall, in Lombard street, between Seventh and Eighth Sts. ... Tickets can be had at Rev. E. Weaver's Book Store, No. 619 Pine street.

articles.headline: History of the African M. E. Church, by Bishop Payne
articles.summary: The bishop requests us to state, that he is prepared to put into our hands for publication, the first volume of that very interesting work -- The History of the African M. E. Church.
people: bishop; author of the History (printed 'Bishop Payne')

articles.headline: City Items
articles.summary: We had a very pleasant time at the two quarterly meetings, last Sabbath, at Camden, New Jersey, under the pastoral care of Rev. J. Woodlin, who is in charge of Bethel church, Phila.; also, Zion Mission, under the pastoral charge of Rev. Stephen Smith. ... We are sorry to learn that Rev. Mr. Gibbs, pastor of Seventh Street Presbyterian church, was so indisposed as not to be able to fill his appointments on the last Sabbath. ... a verdict of guilty, against one of the old citizens and preachers of the Church. ... two of our Bishops in the city ... Revs. Bishops Nazrey and Payne. -- Last night Bethel Sabbath School repeated their exhibition ... One little boy from Zion mission ... delivered the closing piece. ... The small-pox has been very bad in some parts of our city during the winter.
people: in charge of Bethel church, Phila., and of Camden, N.J. (Rev.)

articles.headline: War! War! War! (editorial)
articles.summary: At last the War has burst forth like a mighty tornado, and the most intense excitement pervades the country ... The Confederate army has battered Fort Sumter almost into a blackened mass of ruins, and taken Major Anderson, its brave commander, prisoner. ... But what is the cause of all this tumult? Is it really the Negro? No! We wish here to correct what we conceive to be a very great error in the minds of many of our white friends.

articles.headline: Daughters of Temperance (editorial notice of Hope Grand Union)
articles.summary: In another column of our paper will be found the advertisement, for one year, of Hope Grand Union of the Daughters of Temperance, of the State of Pennsylvania. We were somewhat astonished when a Committee of Ladies waited on us and informed us of such a praiseworthy society. This society was organized in 1840 [VERIFY], and has been the means of doing much good. ... any one wishing to make application will apply to Mrs. H. M. Bunday [VERIFY], G. P. S., No. 814 South Street, or to Mrs. Jane T. Black [VERIFY], No. 612 [VERIFY] Barclay street, or Mrs. E. A. Clark, No. 500 South Fifth street, who is Scribe, or Eliza Bowen [VERIFY], Sydney street, near Coates. We hope that the young men of Philadelphia will take hold and form themselves into a Temperance Society.

articles.headline: Death of Sister Hooper
articles.summary: Died, in Philadelphia, April 15th, 1861, Mrs. Priscilla R. Hooper. She was a sister of the eminently skilful Dr. Wilson, of this city, located at No. 838 [VERIFY] Lombard Street, whose fame as a family physician is better known than we can describe. ... As a literary woman, and as a teacher, she stood high. It is said that whenever she was examined as a teacher, that those who were to be examined at the same time, white and colored, felt ashamed on hearing her prompt answers. Her remains were interred on the 18th inst., at 3 o'clock, P.M.

articles.headline: To Our Subscribers / Our Paper (editorials)
articles.summary: We call upon those of our Burlington, Bristol, West Chester, and Wilmington subscribers, and all others, who have not yet paid their subscriptions ... We lose some twenty-five or thirty dollars from the Baltimore district, on account of all communication being cut off, the bridges having been burnt, etc. ... If our sisters in other places would unite together like the Philadelphia sisters are doing, and give social entertainments for the support of our paper, we would very soon have a small capital on hand.

articles.headline: On Behalf of 'The Recorder'
articles.summary: A Committee of Ladies, belonging to Bethel A. M. E. Church, have undertaken to do something towards the support of the Recorder. This congregation and its Pastor, Rev. Joshua Woodlin, have all along been very active on behalf of our paper. These ladies are energetic and untiring, and their age, experience, and influence promise good results. ... Therefore they propose to give, for the benefit of the Recorder, a Grand Social Entertainment on the First of May, at the Philadelphia Institute, in Lombard street, between Seventh and Eighth streets.
people: pastor, Bethel A. M. E. Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Entertainments (Recorder entertainment; Central Presbyterian gift enterprise)
articles.summary: We hope to see a full house on the First of May, at the Philadelphia Institute. Our ladies will hold there a Social Entertainment for the benefit of the Christian Recorder. ... Tickets only ten cents. The good Ladies of the Central Presbyterian Church will hold a Gift Enterprise in the Vestry of their church, in Lombard street, between Eighth and Ninth streets, on Wednesday evening, May 1st. The proceeds are to go towards fixing up their church, by the time their pastor returns from college. Tickets 25 cents.

articles.headline: Wilberforce University
articles.summary: Bishop Payne has handed us a portion of a letter which he lately received from Rev. Mr. Rust, President of Wilberforce University. ... 'We have the largest number of pupils that we ever had, one hundred, and we are in the midst of a glorious revival. ... Brother Hagan is the leader of the host.'

articles.headline: The Philadelphia Institute for Colored Youth (commencement notice)
articles.summary: The Commencement, or Examination of the pupils, of this Institute will take place on next Friday, May 3d. From the knowledge we have of Prof. Bassett and the other Teachers of the Institute, and their capability for instruction, we bespeak a good audience of literary minds to hear the examination.

articles.headline: Exhibition (St. Thomas' Episcopal Sunday School)
articles.summary: St. Thomas' Episcopal Sunday School repeated their exhibition on last Thursday evening, the 25th inst. The little misses and boys had a very nice meeting. A silver plate, butter dish, and waiter was presented to the Superintendent, Mr. Douglass.

articles.headline: The Star-Spangled Banner, and the Duty of Colored Americans to That Flag (editorial)
articles.summary: The hour brings the men. The man was made to meet the hour. But some men know not their hour nor their day. They know not how to control a trying circumstance for the national good. We must both pity and pray for such. Eighty-six years ago, when the thunder of the Revolution first pealed in the heavens ... where were the men of color? Right by their country's side.

articles.summary: We have received a letter from Rev. James Holloo [VERIFY], of Columbia Circuit, Pa. It brings distressing news. The church at Marietta has been burnt by an infuriated mob. ... [April 21], between two and three o'clock, P.M. ... He was sixty-one years old when he died. (Also: Rev. Daniel Cooper, of New Richmond, Ohio, appointed to that charge by the Ohio Conference.)

articles.headline: City News
articles.summary: On Sabbath morning, we accompanied Rev. John Cornish to his Quarterly Meeting in Germantown. We took the cars, at the corner of Ninth and Green streets... Brother Hall, a local preacher of the Union Church, preached... The Rev. J. Woodlin's Quarterly Meeting came off on the 28th ult. Last night, the 29th, was the Love Feast... The Rev. Mr. Woodlin's lady has been very sick... The ladies' entertainment came off last night, Wednesday, the 1st inst. ... Bethel choir was on hand... What was realized for the Recorder, we are not yet prepared to say.

articles.headline: Personal
articles.summary: Rev. Bishop Nazrey, who has been travelling quite extensively through his diocese, is now at home... Bishop Payne has gone to the New York District. His address will be for awhile in Brooklyn. Rev. J. P. Campbell, our predecessor, was in our book room on Tuesday, the 30th... We are glad to learn that sister Campbell, his wife, is getting better... In some portions of our city, the streets are crowded from morning till night. All are anxious to learn all the particulars in relation to the war between the Unionists and the Seceders.

articles.headline: The General Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- her action relative to publishing a weekly paper and a monthly magazine
articles.summary: We have heard it stated several times, that the General Conference refused to have a weekly paper and a monthly magazine. We have been silent, to a certain degree, in relation to any publication. We must acknowledge that we have been astonished at some things that have been said.

articles.headline: Advice to Our People
articles.summary: Good is admirable... We most respectfully recommend to those of our people in large cities, who are without homes and permanent situations, to go to the country and work on farms... Stephen Smith, Mr. Vidal [VERIFY; printed 'Videl'?], Mr. William Scott, Mr. Henry Gordon, Mr. Ryley, bootmaker, and such women as Mrs. Hawkins [VERIFY], Mrs. Wilkins, and some hundreds more who are in very good business, we have no objections; but there are hundreds who are not doing anything...

The Exercises begin at 9 o'clock, A.M., and, with one recess, will be continued until 6 o'clock, P.M. Classes will be exercised throughout the day, by the teachers as follows...

articles.headline: Advertisement (editorial puff for James Downs)
articles.summary: Our list of advertisement keeps swelling larger and larger. We are glad to have the pleasure of putting in one of the columns of our paper, our friend, Mr James Downs [printed 'Dowes'/'Howes' here, 'DOWNS' in the ad], who formerly kept his second hand clothing store in a cellar, No 29 South Second St., has now fitted up a handsome room, in a good location, at No 296 [VERIFY] South Second St. We hope he may receive a liberal patronage. We yet hope to live to see the Christian Recorder in the family of every colored person in the city of Philadelphia...

articles.headline: Our Religious Exchanges and the War
articles.summary: Our religious exchanges came filled with the war spirit this week, all in for the right of revolution and the suppression of tyranny. We are sorry that our mother State, North Carolina, has paired off from the Stars and Stripes...

articles.headline: Obituary (Mason Mitchell)
articles.author: M. S.
articles.summary: Died, May the 2d, at his residence, near Mount Holly, Mason Mitchell. His age is not exactly known, but our long acquaintance with the deceased proves that he was past the meridian of life. He had been a member of the Methodist Church for thirty-five years. During the most of that time he filled the office of a Trustee... He leaves a wife and five children to mourn his loss. His funeral took place on Sabbath.

It is to be hoped that we will have a good time... We also hope that the brethren will come up with the two cent money strongly.

articles.headline: Our Paper (editorial)
articles.summary: We would say to all who desire to subscribe for the Recorder, that those who will pay us one dollar down, we will send them the paper until the first of January, at which time we will expect all to renew their subscriptions, besides swelling the list to some three thousand or more.

articles.headline: The Philadelphia Annual Conference (editorial)
articles.summary: This Conference adjourned on the 29th ult. We had the pleasure of being at its opening for the first time, being now a member. We have, for the last four or five years, visited the Conference during some stage of its action, and used to think that it was the most unruly Conference that we ever saw; but her last meeting has, no doubt, made up for the past.

articles.headline: Our New Editor of the Christian Recorder
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: In the 23d Number of our paper may be found, in one of its columns, the name of an editor and a corps of regular contributors, or, rather, correspondents, which seem to have struck many of our subscribers, who have stood by us from the beginning of our labors up to the present time, with great astonishment; and we have been asked, How comes, and what is the meaning of this? ... Much of the burden is taken off of us by our Reverend brother, A. L. Stanford, who is stationed at Little Wesley A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia. He is a young man of no ordinary ability, and is much beloved by all who know him. He is associated with us for the ensuing year, and all articles for the Recorder must be directed, when he enters upon his field of labor, to box 430 [VERIFY], Philadelphia, Pa.
people: associate editor of the Recorder for the ensuing year; stationed at Little Wesley A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia (Rev.)

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth -- meeting of parents (address on parental co-operation)
events.location: High School Rooms, 716 & 718 Lombard street, Philadelphia
events.description: Held 'last Thursday evening' (computed 1861-04-04) by invitation of the teachers, for the parents of pupils. About 8 o'clock Mrs. Sarah M. Douglass, 'long known in this community as a successful teacher' and for some years connected with the Institute, stated that the audience had been invited to hear an address to parents, since without parental co-operation the teachers' labors would fail; she then read an address written by Mr. Charles Northend, of Mass. [white educator; not linked]. Points: slight excuses on which pupils are kept from school, want of punctuality and tardiness. Afterward Professor Bassett, 'the efficient Principal of the Institute' [bare surname as printed; = Ebenezer D. Bassett, not linked], delivered an address on the advantages of education and the duties parents owe their children.

events.name: Meeting in support of The Christian Recorder
events.location: [place lost to film damage; Nathaniel Wiggins' letter (CR 1861-04-13 p2) places Stephen Smith's remarks 'at a recent meeting held at our mother-church, Bethel']
events.description: Opened by Rev. J. Woodlin with prayer, singing and remarks about the Recorder; the choir sang a chant. Speeches by brother A. Fields (why the Recorder ought to be supported); by Rev. C. Woodyard [VERIFY initial], who argued it ought to be supported by our people rather than the Public Ledger; by brother Josiah Weir [VERIFY given name], of Union church, that the Christian Recorder is the organ of the Church; by Rev. Stephen Smith, who spoke very warmly on behalf of sustaining the Recorder, 'that it might live and never die'; and by 'our excellent friend, P. S. Smith'. Singing by the choir between speeches. A collection of Ten Dollars and Six Cents was made as a free-will offering.

events.name: Social, Civil and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania -- meeting on the war (Card)
events.location: Office of J. C. White, Philadelphia (per the manuscript minutes)
events.description: CARD. A meeting of the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the colored people of Pennsylvania was held on the 22d inst. [22 April 1861, confirmed by the manuscript minutes], to deliberate upon the alarming condition of the public peace, and to take such measures as the circumstances of the colored people of this State may seem, in our judgment, to demand, and best serve the cause of freedom to man. Formidable difficulties prevent our service being made available to the country in this time of its extremity. First, the laws of this State debar 10,000 able-bodied colored citizens from bearing arms in defence of the State, notwithstanding we have served the Government faithfully as soldiers, artisans and laborers upon every battle field in the country's history... The second is, that the 10,000 colored citizens of this State are not invited, at this stage, by the Government, to enroll themselves; still, in view of the present danger threatening the Commonwealth, we earnestly recommend that the colored citizens stand prepared, so that when officially solicited by the Government we may render such service as only men can render, who know how precious Liberty is. Signed: Isaiah C. Wears, C. Miller, J. P. Clay, William Still, S. M. Smith, J. C. White, Sr., Stephen Smith, Charles H. Bustill, J. P. Worthington, Jonathan C. Gibbs, Morris Brown, P. T. Smith, M. Wheeler. || MANUSCRIPT RECORD: CAVEAT: This is an AI transcription of the actual meeting minutes referenced in the Christian Recorder article. Please reference the actual pictures to validate the transcription. Minutes of the Social, Civil and Statistical Association, Leon Gardiner Collection, Historical Society of Pennsylvania (vol. 27, pp. 264-268). The Executive Committee met at the office of J. C. White on Monday evening, April 22, 1861, Mr. Clay presiding with Wm. Still as secretary, 'in consequence of the present state of public affairs.' A member reported an article he had heard read. William Still opposed any action by 'our people' at this time, since it would turn against them the papers that had been their friends, as with the Bulletin. Mr. Wears favored organizing and drilling so as to 'hold ourselves ready when called on,' and wanted the Bulletin article answered. J. C. White moved 'that in the opinion of this Com. the present time is inopportune for our people, from their peculiar situation, to take any active part in the present crisis.' Rev. Stephen Smith and Rev. J. C. Gibbs offered amendments; Gibbs's held that the Bulletin article was a 'hoax', lest 'Messrs Bowers & Green' be told they had been 'hoaxed' if they applied to those papers again. S. Morgan Smith asked to have his dissent recorded: while opposed to any display, he thought 'our people should in a quiet way express themselves as to their sympathies' and petition the Legislature 'for the right to bear arms' and, if necessary, form home regiments; interrupted by questions from Wears and White and by Gibbs, he sat down and declined to continue. The matter was referred to a committee (on April 29 identified as Gibbs's Civil Rights Committee) with instructions to report. The minutes also refer to a meeting 'convened at the Masonic Hall on the evening of the 22nd'. At the April 29 meeting, again at White's office, Still moved that Rev. J. C. Gibbs chair; White corrected the minutes (he had not interrupted Smith), and Gibbs disclaimed any hostile feeling toward Smith; Gibbs, as chairman of the Civil Rights Committee, then read this Card, 'which had been published by the Com. in all the principal daily papers.' Minutes signed S. Morgan Smith, Secretary. Photographs of the minutes taken by Michiko Quinones at HSP, pp. 264-268: manuscripts/SCSA_minutes_1861/HSP_LGC_v27_p264.jpg manuscripts/SCSA_minutes_1861/HSP_LGC_v27_p265.jpg manuscripts/SCSA_minutes_1861/HSP_LGC_v27_p266.jpg manuscripts/SCSA_minutes_1861/HSP_LGC_v27_p267.jpg manuscripts/SCSA_minutes_1861/HSP_LGC_v27_p268.jpg NOTE (Michiko, 2026-10-31): S. Morgan Smith is the same man as Rev. Stephen Smith. The Card prints both 'S. M. Smith' and 'Stephen Smith' among the signers, and the minutes name 'Rev. Stephen Smith' (who offered an amendment) and 'S. Morgan Smith' (the secretary, who recorded his dissent) separately; both are linked to the one person.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A.M.E. Church, 1861 -- proceedings, 18-23 May
events.location: Union Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Saturday 18 May, 9 A.M.: Bishop Nazrey presided; Revs. J. Woodlin and W. D. W. Schureman appointed Secretaries; on motion of Rev. J. P. Campbell, Rev. E. Weaver appointed Reporter for the Christian Recorder and some weekly papers; on motion of Rev. E. Weaver, Rev. J. P. Campbell appointed Reporter for the daily papers; financial reports called for; Bishop's remarks; 'the appointments were announced' [i.e. of the Conference committees -- the pastoral appointments list is NOT printed in this issue]; adjourned to Monday. Monday 20 May: Bishop Nazrey in the chair; opened by Rev. J. P. Campbell; on his motion the rules of the General Conference adopted with alterations; reports from brethren; a Committee on Finance and a Bishop's Committee appointed. Tuesday 21 May: opened by Rev. James Hollon [VERIFY] by reading and singing; finance reports; the Bishop's annual address (extempore): had travelled through the district, attended Quarterly Conferences without presiding, referred to his letters in the Recorder; some circuits have five or six appointments with preaching only once in five or six weeks; Conference delayed several days by charges against brethren that were really complaints of indebtedness; 'Many of the brethren look for an appointment like the Bethel and Union charges, but the best way is for a minister to make his own appointment good'; rules wanted for examining candidates; the new Book of Discipline; the General Conference had taken the Book Concern out of this body's hands and put it in a General Committee. Wednesday 22 May: Bishop Nazrey, assisted by Bishop Payne; opened by brother Schureman; complaints against brethren disposed of; right of brother J. P. B. Eddy to take part questioned, he said he would remain silent; charges referred to committees; at noon a ten-minute recess for lunch which 'the good sisters of Union Church' prepare every day in the vestry; committees on various subjects appointed; question four on page 82 [VERIFY] of the new Discipline taken up. Thursday 23 May: Bishop Nazrey assisted by Bishop Payne; opened by brother Woodlin; committees on ordination and on letters and petitions reported; disciplinary question; voted to hold the next Annual Conference at Trenton, New Jersey; adjourned to Friday 9 A.M. (continued in a later issue).
